newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen, BellSouth in talks - sources.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen, BellSouth in talks - sources.

text.p: German steel and engineering group Thyssen AG and Atlanta-based BellSouth Corp. are involved in intensive talks over setting up a new telecommunications venture, sources close to the talks said Friday.

If the talks prove successful, Thyssen could emerge from its current position as an also-ran in the race to compete with German telecommunications monopoly Deutsche Telekom AG as a strong challenger in a market expected to be worth more than 100 billion marks ($64.2 billion) in four years.

The talks between Thyssen and BellSouth centre on relaunching an earlier plan to set up a jointly-held company that would offer comprehensive telecommunication services in Germany when markets are deregulated in 1998.

The new twist is that Thyssen and BellSouth would merge their stakes in E-Plus Mobilfunk GmbH, Germany's No. 3 cellular phone group, into the new company and thereby give their new venture a dominant majority in E-Plus.

This would make it possible for the Thyssen-BellSouth venture to exert broad influence over E-Plus as the main technical platform on which to launch telecommunications services to both business and residential customers.
"BellSouth has decided to strengthen its activities in E-Plus considerably," an industry source close to the talks said on condition of anonymity.
"Thyssen and BellSouth are in the process of setting up a much broader relationship in telecommunications and are now engaged in intensive negotiations," the source added.
Thyssen declined official comment and no comment was immediately available from BellSouth's European offices.
Thyssen holds a 30.1 percent stake in E-Plus and BellSouth owns around 22.5 percent. The other large shareholder in the mobile phone group is German energy group Veba AG.
